error_analysis.trigger: recording 1302664060426140_0001_3375_22000 scored worse-than-chance zero-shot AUROC on ALL 7 channels simultaneously in zero_shot_channel_matrix_train_val.json
error_analysis.method: audit self-speech vs other-speech RMS ratio, computed directly from RTTM segment boundaries and RAW audio (no model), across every recording in the internal train+val pool (172 recordings). A wearer-worn mic should show SELF ('0') louder than OTHER ('1') on average (near-field proximity gain); this checks whether the flagged recording is a real acoustic outlier or a role-swap.
error_analysis.interpretation: Exactly 1 of 172 recordings has a self/other RMS ratio below 0.5 (1302664060426140_0001_3375_22000, ratio=0.214), more than 3x lower than the next-lowest recording, against a population median ratio of 1.94. This uniform, severe, single-recording inversion (worse-than-chance AUROC on every one of 7 independent microphones) is the signature of a SPEAKER-ROLE LABEL SWAP in that recording's official RTTM, not a genuine acoustic hard case or a GeoWearNet model failure. Per campaign rules, the raw MMCSG RTTM is NOT modified; this is recorded as a known, isolated (1/172) label-quality defect. It is not excluded from already-computed aggregate metrics (which are frame-count-weighted over many recordings, so one mislabeled ~3-minute recording has a small, diluted effect on pooled AUROC) but should be kept in mind if this specific recording ever dominates a small-n analysis (e.g. a single-recording qualitative demo).

pareto_spec.rationale: solo AUROC is the campaign's mandatory primary discrimination metric; false-wearer-rate-on-environment-only is the direct upstream cause of bystander leakage, the product's first-class failure mode. Parameter count and context length break ties on the deployment budget (CPU, on-device, streaming).
